answer: I would like to talk about someone in my own family whose parenting I genuinely admire. A person I consider an excellent parent is my elder sister, and watching her raise her two children has been a real education. She lives in Dhaka with her husband and children, including a lively four-year-old son, and we see them whenever they visit Sirajganj or I go to stay with them. As for how she raises them, what impresses me is how she balances warmth with [[discipline]]; she is affectionate but never lets her children become spoiled. She listens to them genuinely, treating even their small worries as important, which I think builds real trust. Rather than simply giving orders, she explains the reasons behind rules, so her children grow up thinking for themselves. She limits their screen time, reads to them every night and makes sure they spend plenty of time with their grandparents, which I think matters enormously. She is also remarkably [[patient]], even on the difficult days when most people would lose their temper. As for why I think she is a good parent, what I admire most is that she leads by example, modelling the values she wants them to [[absorb]]. I think parenting is one of the hardest jobs in the world, and she makes it look almost effortless. Honestly, her children are turning out kind and confident, which is the clearest possible proof of her [[nurturing]] approach. I suspect our mother taught her more than she realises.

followUps.q: Do you think you would be a good parent?
followUps.answer: I hope so. I think I would be patient and fair, like my sister, but I would probably struggle with discipline because I tend to give in too easily. I would definitely ask her for [[guidance]].

followUps.q: Do parents today have an easier job than in the past?
followUps.answer: In some ways yes, with more information and support available. But they also face new pressures, like managing screen time and intense competition in education, which makes parenting quite demanding.
